Note attack_ica.py's main() defaults to epsilon=1e-2, the leakiest setting measured (81/81 directions shrunk below 0.99, 47 below 0.5); the whiten.py default of 1e-3 is better but still leaks. Recommendation: release k=64 PCA-truncated, exactly whitened features. That gives Cov(z) = I exactly (zero second-order leak), no amplified junk, discards <1e-4 of variance per dropped direction, AND additionally kills the discrete-support attack (#13), because the coarse-quantisation directions are precisely the ones truncated away (corner pixel 0 takes only NINE distinct values across all 60,000 images, versus 45,021 for interior pixel 40 -- a signature that survives exact whitening but not truncation).

3. Rotation-only is not a defence and should be included only as a control. For an informed attacker it is a single closed-form matrix product (Q = Vhat U^T from two eigendecompositions); the pool's top-20 relative eigen-gaps are 37%, 14%, 7.1%, 7.6%, 24%, 21%, 18%, 5.8%, 9.1%, 23%, ... with only two below 3%, against a 1.0% sampling error at n=20k, so the recovery is essentially exact. Answer to organizer question (1): whitening is NECESSARY (it removes the cheap second-order attack, which is otherwise a one-liner) but NOT SUFFICIENT (the strongest attacks are affine-equivariant and do not care).

4. Separate train/test whitening: do not do it. It is a pure loss. Security gain: zero -- the attacker whitens the released data themselves, so whitening is attacker-reproducible by construction and hiding it changes nothing. Honest-learner cost, measured by split-half at n=10,000: PCA eigenvectors are catastrophically unstable, with 9 of the top 40 split-half overlaps below 0.9 and several at 0.65-0.69 (40-50 degree rotations) plus arbitrary sign flips -- separate-PCA is a broken task, not a defence variant. ZCA is the continuous alternative: relative operator-norm mismatch ||W_A - W_B||/||W_pool|| = 4.4%, and the train-ZCA applied to test data yields a covariance with top eigenvalue 1.19 instead of 1.0, i.e. a small but real distribution shift the learner cannot correct from released data. There is also a perverse incentive: to recover that loss an honest entrant must estimate the train/test alignment by unsupervised distribution matching over O(81), which is literally the attack machinery. And the intuitive worry that separate whitening leaks MORE is, I believe, wrong: if the release is exactly white, the fold/sample covariance fluctuations are Wishart(I), whose distribution is orthogonally invariant and therefore carries zero bits about Q. Use one joint map, fitted on the pool, published in the protocol. Answer to organizer question (2): joint.

5. THE STRUCTURAL RESULT the whole study should be framed around. No invertible linear release map can prevent feature smuggling, for the same reason the organizer already knows linear models are invariant: for any frozen nonlinear f trained offline, the class {f(Mz + b) : M invertible} contains f(x) exactly, since M = A^{-1}, b = mu is in the class. A smuggled pretrained CNN plus a LEARNED 81x81 adapter is exactly as expressive under every variant here; the release only charges the attacker 6561 extra parameters (3240 if they exploit the published W and constrain M to the Stiefel manifold), which 10,000 labelled rows pay easily. Whitening and rotation change the PRICE of smuggling, not its POSSIBILITY. The right experimental question is therefore not "can the pixel basis be recovered" but "what does recovery cost in joules and in accuracy, relative to the honest path" -- E1/E2 should report joules, and E4 should report the honest-vs-smuggled gap at each accuracy band.

6. Two protocol holes that dominate all the cryptanalysis. (a) whiten.py uses a single fixed DEFAULT_ROTATION_SEED, so A is CONSTANT across every draw and every entrant. Crack it once offline with unlimited compute and smuggle A^{-1}: 81x81 int8 with per-row float16 scales is 6.72 KB binary, ~9.0 KB base64, comfortably inside the 20 KB cap (float16 is 13.1 KB / 17.5 KB base64, also fits). The defence's security level is "one determined entrant, once". Q must be redrawn per scored evaluation, and no practice/dev phase may share the final Q. (b) Exact-source draws are unconditionally fatal, and worse than the organizer's note suggests: because W is pool-derived and the protocol is published, the attacker recomputes W exactly, so ||z|| = ||W(x-mu)|| is an exact invariant they can compute offline; match ~81-200 rows by norm and orthogonal Procrustes gives Q EXACTLY, after which all 20,000 rows are in pixel space. Partial overlap is enough -- 0.1% of the draw suffices for Procrustes. So the hold-out draw must have literally zero overlap with anything derivable from public 9x9 data, and E2 should measure the overlap threshold at which Procrustes stops working. Also audit: does the scored container have network access or MNIST on disk? If so the 20 KB cap is decorative.

7. Measurement design warnings for E1/E2. (i) mean_peak_energy_fraction is the WRONG headline metric. ICA on digit images converges to localised edge/blob filters, not pixels, so this metric will look reassuring while the attack has already succeeded for the attacker's purpose -- a basis of localised filters plus a recovered adjacency is nearly as good as pixels for a CNN. Add a localisation metric that credits localised-but-not-pixel filters (spatial second moment or participation ratio of each composite row reshaped to 9x9) and always report end-to-end cnn_query_error_pct as the headline. (ii) attack_ica.py's logcosh contrast is the weak attack; the strong contrasts are non-negativity (free, blind) and the known zero-inflated [0,1] marginals (2.6 KB of quantile tables). Report them head to head or the study will under-estimate the threat. (iii) An attacker restarts; report the BEST over seeds and contrasts, not the mean, and check ica_converged_iterations against max_iter so "attack failed" is not confused with "optimiser failed". (iv) Any "we found structure" statistic needs a Wishart(I) / random-rotation null run through the identical pipeline; whiten.composite_controls already does this for one metric and every new metric needs the same. (v) Fix the chance line for adjacency precision at 288/3240 = 0.0889 and put the permuted-pixel release's >=0.99 on the same axis -- the three-way separation (permutation 0.99 / eps>0 above chance / eps=0 and k=64 at chance) is the single clearest figure available.

8. What would actually work, if the goal is to stop precomputed spatial features. Linear obfuscation is the wrong tool -- it is invertible by definition and therefore defeated by an adapter. The options that survive this analysis are: (a) change the DATA rather than the basis, i.e. score on a hold-out 9x9 dataset that no one has a pretrained model for, and accept that the only defence is novelty; (b) make the release non-invertible in a way that destroys spatial structure but preserves label information (random projection to k << 81 with k chosen so a CNN prior no longer helps -- note this also costs honest learners); (c) accept smuggling and PRICE it, scoring energy so that recovery cost counts -- though every attack above costs 1-3 s and a few hundred joules against a 1200 s budget, so this does not currently bite; (d) fresh Q per evaluation plus a zero-overlap hold-out draw, which at least forces the 3240-parameter recovery to happen inside the scored window every time. One useful cheap mitigation that falls out of measurement #13: releasing at reduced precision (rounding z to ~1e-3) costs honest learners essentially nothing and may kill the discrete-support attack; worth a single cell in the experiment grid.

BUDGET NOTE: everything above can be measured on CPU except the end-to-end CNN numbers and the Stiefel/sliced-Wasserstein attack; the full E1-E4 grid should fit in well under 2 GPU-hours, far inside the stated 2-GPU / $10 limit.

flaws.issue: attack_ica.py:217-219 feeds the secret map into the attack. `composite = unmixing @ transform["A"]` uses the organizer's secret A, then `mixing = pinv(composite)`, `scale = norm(mixing, axis=0)`, `sources = sources * scale` rescales the ICA sources by their PIXEL-SPACE synthesis norms before handing them to `topology.recover_layout`. The comment at line 215-216 states this rescale is load-bearing ("without which the second-order topology attack has nothing to work with"). A real blind attacker has only `pinv(unmixing)` column norms, which are in released-z units, not pixel units.
flaws.why_it_matters: E1's headline end-to-end number (lattice recovered -> CNN accuracy) is produced by an attacker holding Q, W and mu. If the defence is declared broken on that basis, the conclusion is wrong; if it is declared safe despite the oracle, that is a valid upper bound but must be labelled as one. Either way the number does not describe any attacker in the threat model.
flaws.fix: Split every module into attacker-side and scorer-side namespaces, and enforce it mechanically: the attacker function signature takes only (z_train, y_train, z_test[, x_pub, y_pub]) and returns its artifacts; A/mu/Q are passed only to scoring functions. Re-run the rescale with an attacker-computable scale (column norms of pinv(unmixing), i.e. z-space) and report both; if the attack only works with the pixel-space scale, that is the finding. The newer attacks.py/run.py already do this correctly (`comp = b @ a` is used only for scoring) - port that discipline and delete the attack_ica.py path rather than keeping two pipelines.

flaws.issue: The experiment never separates "W is published" from "W is secret", yet question (1) has different answers in the two cases. If W (the whitening recipe and its fit set) is part of the published protocol, then whiten+rotate is the composition of a KNOWN invertible map with a secret Q, i.e. information-theoretically identical to rotation-only; the only empirical content left is the eps-floor tail and the honest-utility cost. If W is secret (fitted on the draw's rows and never published), it is a weak secret that the attacker re-estimates from the released data itself up to a rotation. VARIANTS in common.py encodes neither choice.
flaws.why_it_matters: Question (1) - "is rotation alone enough, or do I need decorrelation first?" - cannot be answered by the measurement as designed, because the two arms differ by a quantity whose secrecy status is undefined. The already-computed exact-* results show this dominating everything: exact-zca1e-3+rot-s1 gives 99.93% label recovery when the attacker refits W on the pool (matching the organizer) and 15.53% when he refits on the wrong rows. That 84-point swing is entirely about W's secrecy, not about whitening.
flaws.fix: Add an explicit protocol axis `w_public in {True, False}` and run every attack in both settings. In `w_public=True`, have the attacker apply the published W^-1 to the released data before attacking, which should make 'rot' and 'zca+rot' statistically indistinguishable - state that as a prediction and test it as an equivalence (see the protocol below). Publish the answer as "whitening adds security only if the fit set is secret, and then only <X> bits".

flaws.issue: attacks.informed_attack can fail for optimisation reasons and the experiment has no way to tell that apart from the defence working. It optimises 3240 Stiefel parameters (`free` 81x81 via matrix_exp) with 600 Adam steps at lr 2e-3 from at most three inits, reports `init_loss` and `final_loss`, and never reports the moment-matching loss evaluated at the TRUE R (which the scorer can compute from the secret A).
flaws.why_it_matters: A failed attack is not evidence of security. If final_loss is far above the loss at the true R, the correct conclusion is "my optimiser is weak", not "whitening+rotation resists informed attackers". Question (3) would then be answered backwards, and the organizer would ship a defence whose only support is an under-tuned Adam run.
flaws.fix: Add `loss_at_truth` to every informed record (scoring-side, computed from the secret A) and report the gap. Add >=5 random restarts and a warm-start control that begins at the truth plus a rotation of angle theta for theta in {5, 15, 45} degrees: if the optimiser cannot stay at the truth, the loss surface, not the defence, is what you measured. Also report a rank/identifiability diagnostic: the number of independent constraints (10 class means + 10 class covariances) versus 3240 unknowns.

flaws.issue: The overlap-world attack stops one step short of the real break. attacks.norm_match_labels only reads labels off matched rows. The far more damaging continuation is never run: match ~1000 rows by norm (already 99.9% accurate for 'rot' and for any variant where the attacker guesses the fit set), then solve Procrustes on the matched (x, z) pairs to recover the full map A exactly, then apply it to every row - including unmatched ones and including the whole test set - and run the offline CNN in the true pixel gauge.
flaws.why_it_matters: This is the attack that decides question (3) and decides whether the held-out draw is optional or mandatory. As currently measured the hole looks like "label lookup, only works if the exact images are in the pool"; the Procrustes continuation shows it also hands over the secret map itself, which then generalises to rows the attacker never matched, and costs a few hundred bytes of submitted code. Measuring the weak version risks the organizer concluding the hole is survivable.
flaws.fix: Add a ~15-line `procrustes_from_matched(z_test, x_pool, matched_idx)` attack: estimate A_hat by least squares on the matched pairs, report ||A_hat - A||/||A||, the pixel rel-RMS on UNMATCHED rows, and the smuggled-CNN accuracy on those unmatched rows. Sweep the number of matched anchors (50, 200, 1000) to find the minimum. Run it against every variant.

flaws.issue: stage_exact conflates "the norm-matching attack works" with "the attacker guessed the organizer's whitening fit set". It builds the release with W fitted on `x` (pool) or `x[tr]` (train) but always lets the attacker refit on the full pool. There is no matched-knowledge arm for the train-fit release.
flaws.why_it_matters: The existing numbers (99.93 vs 15.53, 99.93 vs 16.05) are reported as if they were a property of the variant, but they are a property of the fit-set mismatch. A reader will conclude "fit W on the train rows and the exact-source hole closes", which is false: the attacker can estimate the train-row whitening from the released train features themselves (Cov(z_train) tells him W Sigma_tr W^T), and can always search over the small set of plausible fit sets.
flaws.fix: Add the matched arm (attacker refits on the same rows the organizer used, where those rows are public) and an adaptive arm where the attacker estimates the scale factor per direction from the released covariance before matching norms. Report all three. Also replace the single-scalar norm match with norm-shortlist + verification against distances to 2-3 already-identified anchors, which removes the collision failures that currently cap the attack.

flaws.issue: No attack is costed against the 20 KB submission size cap, which is the organizer's actual binding defence. attacks.informed_attack needs `x_pub` (40000 x 81 float32 = 13 MB) at runtime; even compressed to sufficient statistics it needs mu_pub (324 B), Sigma_pub^{1/2} (26 KB float32), 10 class means (3.2 KB) and 10 class covariances (262 KB float32). That is 10x-600x over the cap.
flaws.why_it_matters: An attack that cannot be shipped is not an attack. Conversely, the unpermute demo already proved that a 1.8 KB artifact suffices against the permutation defence, so the organizer's correct question is not "is the attack possible" but "does it survive compression to 20 KB". Measuring only the uncompressed attack answers neither the pass nor the fail case.
flaws.fix: Add a `bytes` field to every attack record and a quantised variant of each attack: int8 class means, class covariances in a shared 20-30 dim eigenbasis, Sigma_pub^{1/2} as its top-k eigenpairs in int8. Report attack success as a function of artifact size (0.5, 2, 20 KB). If whitening+rotation forces the attacker over 20 KB, that IS the defence and it should be stated that way.

flaws.issue: Seeding conflates the two sources of variance and there are too few of them. common.release derives Q from `seed * 7919 + 17` and common.draw derives the row split from the same `seed`, so Q cannot be varied with the draw held fixed. run.py defaults to 3 seeds, results are single numbers, and no stage reports a confidence interval or a paired difference.
flaws.why_it_matters: Attack outcomes here are bimodal (the lattice is either recovered or it is not), so 3 draws gives a success-rate estimate with roughly +/-30% binomial width - useless for a security decision. Worse, a security claim must be about the WORST Q an entrant could face, not the mean; with Q locked to the draw you cannot even estimate the spread over Q.
flaws.fix: Split the seed into `draw_seed` and `rotation_seed` (independent streams). Use 3 draws x 5 Q per draw = 15 security cells and report the fraction of cells where the attack succeeds with a Wilson interval, plus the max-over-Q attack success. Use 3 draws x 3 model seeds for honest utility and report paired per-draw differences against the 'raw' arm, not absolute accuracies.

flaws.issue: Honest-utility measurements are confounded by optimiser conditioning and by a basis-dependent regulariser. models.mlp_fit_predict uses fixed lr=2e-3, 30 epochs, OneCycle, AdamW wd=1e-4 for every release, but raw pixels and ZCA-whitened features differ in Gram condition number by many orders of magnitude. models.logreg_fit_predict uses `LogisticRegression(C=1.0)`, whose L2 penalty is NOT invariant under an invertible linear change of basis.
flaws.why_it_matters: E3 and E4 are supposed to isolate the accuracy cost of whitening and of separate-vs-joint fitting. As written, any observed difference is indistinguishable from "the fixed learning rate suited one conditioning better" and, for the linear model, from "the ridge penalty was measured in a different basis". The known fact that linear models are exactly invariant to invertible linear maps holds only unregularised; the code's logreg will show a spurious variant effect and the write-up will misattribute it.
flaws.fix: For the MLP, sweep lr over {5e-4, 2e-3, 8e-3} per variant and report the per-variant best (and report the spread - if the spread exceeds the variant effect, say so). For the linear model, run unregularised (C=1e6) or LBFGS-to-convergence as the invariance check - it must give identical accuracy across all invertible variants, and if it does not, the pipeline has a bug. Keep the C=1 run only as a separately labelled "regularisation is basis-dependent" demonstration.

flaws.issue: The metrics measure basis recovery, not usable-feature recovery, and the blind stage never applies the smuggled artifact. stage_blind reports matched energy, localisation and edge precision, then trains a FRESH CNN on the draw's own 10k labelled rows over the recovered layout. The smuggled offline CNN is applied only in stage_informed.
flaws.why_it_matters: Basis recovery and smuggling come apart in both directions. A 60%-matched-energy reconstruction is a blurred pixel image, which a shift-augmented offline CNN tolerates well (so a mediocre basis score can still be a total break); conversely a perfect layout over unit-variance ICA sources is in the wrong gauge and the offline CNN will not transfer (so a perfect basis score can be harmless). The organizer asked about precomputed features, so the decision metric must be the offline artifact's test error, not a geometry score.
flaws.fix: Report three end-to-end numbers per cell: (a) offline CNN applied to the attacker's pixel estimate, (b) fresh in-competition CNN on the recovered layout, (c) honest MLP on the released features - all as test error, on the same draw and the same seeds. Add the oracle control: the same fresh CNN on the sources arranged by the TRUE peak-pixel layout (scorer-side). Without (c) you cannot say whether the attack helped; without the oracle you cannot tell a layout-recovery failure from a "conv on ICA sources does not work at all" failure.

flaws.issue: common.basis_recovery_report (line 137-142) documents "on active pixels only" but never filters: it runs Hungarian matching over all 81 columns, including the ~6-18 always-black border pixels whose energy assignment is arbitrary. attack_ica.matching_report does take an `active` argument and stage_blind does not pass one.
flaws.why_it_matters: The dead pixels are free columns in the assignment problem, so matched_energy_mean and n_above_0.5 are systematically distorted (typically inflated, because junk sources get parked on junk pixels at high normalised energy). Every cross-variant comparison of those numbers is off by an unknown amount, and pca60 (60 rows vs 81 columns) is distorted differently from the 81-dim variants.
flaws.fix: Pass the active mask (pool variance > 1e-4, computed from the public rows) into basis_recovery_report and restrict both rows and columns to it; report n_active alongside. Re-derive the same number on the dead columns as a null.

flaws.issue: The eps variance floor - which whiten.py's own docstring identifies as the one real design decision and an explicit second-order leak - is never probed by a second-order-only attack, and VARIANTS contains no eps=0 arm. With a floor, Cov(z) = Q diag(lam/(lam+eps)) Q^T is not the identity, so the low-variance subspace (near axis-aligned blank-border directions in pixel space) is directly identifiable from the released covariance alone, with no ICA and no labels.
flaws.why_it_matters: This is the cheapest possible attack on the proposed defence and it takes one eigendecomposition. If it recovers the dead-pixel subspace, the organizer learns that eps must be 0 or that truncation is mandatory - a design decision the current plan simply does not test. The informed 'eig' init touches this obliquely but is entangled with labels and with a 600-step optimiser.
flaws.fix: Add a standalone 10-line blind attack: eigendecompose Cov(z_all), take the bottom-m eigenvectors, and report the principal angles between that subspace and the true dead-pixel subspace (scorer-side), for eps in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} and for pca-k in {60, 70}. Pair it with the honest MLP accuracy at the same eps. Those two curves decide the eps question outright at negligible cost.

flaws.issue: Question (2) is measured only on the cost side. stage_separate compares shared / separate / pool whitening for honest MLP and logreg accuracy, but no attack is ever run against the separate-fit release.
flaws.why_it_matters: The organizer asked whether train and test should be whitened separately. Answering with a cost number alone implies the benefit is positive, which is not established. Separate fitting adds no secret (it is the same recipe on different rows), strictly breaks the honest train->test map, and plausibly HELPS the attacker: it hands him two independent noisy views of the same Q, and fitting the test map on the test rows makes the released test features a function of the test set, which is an extra constraint he can exploit. None of that is measured.
flaws.fix: Run informed_attack and the norm-match/Procrustes attack against the separate-fit release for the same draws, and report attack success for shared vs separate side by side with the honest cost. Also name the out-of-scope option explicitly (a separate Q per split, which destroys honest learning) so the write-up does not leave it ambiguous.

flaws.issue: attack_ica.py:271 monkeypatches the module global `topology.recover_layout` with a lambda that returns a frozen layout, and never restores it.
flaws.why_it_matters: Any later call to topology.recover_layout in the same process - including by `learners` in a subsequent variant or seed within the same run - silently returns the stale layout from an earlier cell. In a loop over variants this produces cross-contaminated results that look plausible and are impossible to spot in the JSON.
flaws.fix: Pass the layout in as a parameter (learners already needs a hook for this) or use contextlib and restore in a finally block. Better: drop attack_ica.py in favour of the attacks.py path, which does not monkeypatch.

flaws.issue: Compute is spent where it does not change any decision. stage_blind runs 4 similarity feeds x 2 unmixers x 120 s QAP per (variant, seed): with 7 variants x 3 seeds that is roughly 6 GPU-free CPU hours of QAP alone, most of it on 'raw-corr' (a known null, since ICA sources are white by construction) and on unmixer/feed combinations whose outcome is decided before the QAP starts. Meanwhile nothing in the study uses a GPU at all (models.DEVICE='cpu', 81-dim data), so the 2-GPU / $10 Modal budget is unnecessary, and the QAP time limit - the free parameter that decides success - is only ever evaluated at a single 120 s point, even though the threat model says the attack must run in seconds inside a scored submission.
flaws.why_it_matters: Wasted wall-clock displaces the seeds the study actually needs (see the seeding flaw), and a single QAP time point cannot answer "is this attack admissible under the scored energy/time ranking". A 120 s attack that then trains a CNN may cost more than the honest MLP it is trying to beat, which would make the attack self-defeating - a result the organizer would very much want, and which the current design cannot produce.
flaws.fix: Keep 'raw-corr' once per variant as a null and drop it elsewhere. Gate the expensive QAP on a cheap attacker-side screen (mutual-kNN graph degree/planarity, or the gap between the top-k and bulk of the similarity matrix); only escalate cells that pass. Replace the single 120 s point with a success-vs-QAP-budget curve at {2, 10, 30, 120} s, and report attack wall-time next to honest-learner wall-time in every record. Run the whole study on the Intel MacBook for $0 and spend the Modal budget, if at all, on a single A100 timing pass for the energy axis.

flaws.issue: 'rot' and 'zca+rot' are measured as two independent expensive arms of the blind attack, when for a blind attacker they are provably the same experiment: FastICA whitens internally (whiten='unit-variance'), and attacks.sparse_nonneg_unmix applies its own ZCA before optimising, so both arms feed the identical whitened cloud into the identical search.
flaws.why_it_matters: Half the blind-stage compute buys a foregone conclusion. Worse, the plan treats the comparison as the answer to question (1), when the blind comparison cannot discriminate the two variants at all - only the informed comparison can (through the eigenvalue spectrum, which whitening destroys and rotation-only preserves).
flaws.fix: Recast the blind 'rot' vs 'zca+rot' comparison as a VALIDITY CHECK rather than a result: run both on the same draws and test for equivalence (paired difference in edge precision and end-to-end error, with a TOST-style interval). If they differ beyond numerical noise, something in the pipeline is broken (most likely the eps floor). Then answer question (1) from the informed arm only, where the 'eig'-init attack should succeed on 'rot' and fail on 'zca+rot' - that single gap is the entire measured value of whitening.

missing_measurements: Moment-matching loss evaluated at the TRUE Stiefel matrix R, alongside init_loss and final_loss, for every informed attack cell - the only way to separate "defence works" from "Adam failed".
Bytes of the attacker's offline artifact for every attack, plus attack success as a function of artifact size (0.5 / 2 / 20 KB quantised), since the 20 KB cap is the real defence.
Attack wall-time and (for the A100 arm) energy, reported next to the honest learner's, so admissibility under the energy/time-at-fixed-accuracy ranking can be judged.

Test error at the competition's accuracy bands (2/3/5/8/12%) rather than a single accuracy at one fixed training recipe; honest and cheating submissions each need a (time, error) point pair at minimum.
Smuggled offline CNN applied to the BLIND attacker's output (currently only applied in the informed stage).
Oracle-layout control: fresh CNN trained on ICA sources arranged by the true peak-pixel layout, to separate layout-recovery failure from "conv over ICA sources is useless".

Second-order-only probe of the eps floor: principal angles between the bottom-m eigenvectors of Cov(z) and the true dead-pixel subspace, for eps in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} and pca-k in {60, 70}, paired with honest MLP accuracy at the same setting.
An eps=0 (exact whitening) variant in common.VARIANTS - the docstring's three-way trade-off is stated but only two corners are instantiated.
Procrustes recovery of A from norm-matched anchor rows, with ||A_hat - A||/||A||, pixel rel-RMS on UNMATCHED rows, and smuggled-CNN accuracy on those rows, as a function of anchor count.
Attack results against the separate-fit (train/test whitened independently) release - currently only the honest cost of separate fitting is measured.

Matched-knowledge arm of the exact-source attack (attacker refits W on exactly the rows the organizer used) and an adaptive arm that estimates the per-direction scaling from Cov(z_train) before norm matching.

Per-variant learning-rate sweep for the honest MLP and an unregularised linear baseline, to make the E3/E4 accuracy deltas attributable to the release map rather than to optimiser conditioning and a basis-dependent L2 penalty.
Active-pixel-restricted versions of matched_energy_mean / n_above_0.5, plus the same statistic on the dead columns as a null.
Variance of attack success over Q with the draw held fixed (requires decoupling rotation_seed from draw_seed), and the max-over-Q value, not just the mean.

Held-out-draw arm: the same attacks run against a 9x9 dataset the attacker's public pool does not contain (e.g. EMNIST-digits or KMNIST resized), which is the only condition under which the informed numbers mean anything.
critic:protocol.recommended_protocol:
ZERO GPU, ZERO MODAL DOLLARS. Every array here is 81-dimensional; models.DEVICE is already 'cpu' and nothing in the study needs an accelerator. Run the whole thing on the Intel MacBook (~7 h wall, overnight). Reserve the $10 / 2-GPU budget solely for an optional final A100 timing+energy pass on the 6 surviving (release, submission) pairs, if the organizer wants the ranking axis in real units; that is <15 min of A100, well under $10.

STRUCTURAL PREREQUISITES (do these before any run; they cost nothing and without them the numbers are uninterpretable):
P1. Decouple seeds: `draw_seed` (row split) and `rotation_seed` (Q) as independent streams in common.draw / common.release.
P2. Enforce the attacker/scorer split: attacker functions take only (z_train, y_train, z_test[, x_pub, y_pub]) and return artifacts; A/W/mu/Q/test-labels reach only scoring functions. Delete the attack_ica.py pixel-space rescale (lines 217-219) and its topology.recover_layout monkeypatch (line 271); keep the attacks.py path as the single pipeline.
P3. Add the protocol axis `w_public in {True, False}`. When True, the attacker applies the published W^-1 before attacking.
P4. Add `bytes` (quantised artifact size) and `seconds` to every attack record; add `loss_at_truth` to every informed record; restrict basis_recovery_report to active pixels.

VARIANTS (7, down from the current cross): raw; rot; zca_eps0+rot; zca_1e-3+rot; zca_1e-2+rot; pca60+rot; zca_1e-3+rot_separate (test whitened on its own rows, same Q). 'perm' and 'zca1e-3' (no rotation) stay only as sanity anchors, one seed each.

SEEDS: 3 draw_seeds x 5 rotation_seeds = 15 security cells per variant; 3 draw_seeds x 3 model_seeds for utility. Report attack success as a fraction over the 15 with a Wilson interval, plus the MAX over Q; report utility as paired per-draw deltas against 'raw'.

STAGE 0 - free algebra checks (2 min total, run first; if any fails, stop, the pipeline is broken):
 (a) Unregularised logistic regression must give bit-identical accuracy on raw / rot / zca+rot for the same draw. If not, there is a numerical or plumbing bug.
 (b) FastICA sources on 'rot' and on 'zca_1e-3+rot' at the same draw must agree to numerical noise (both whiten internally).
 -> These two turn the expensive blind 'rot' vs 'zca+rot' comparison into a validity check rather than a result.

STAGE A - eps-floor second-order probe (5 min, no ICA, no CNN, no labels). For each variant and cell: eigendecompose Cov(z_all); report principal angles between its bottom-m subspace and the true dead-pixel subspace; and honest MLP error at the same setting.
 DECIDES: the eps / truncation design choice. If eps=1e-3 recovers the dead subspace to within a few degrees while eps=0 or pca60 does not, the answer is \"truncate, do not floor\". This alone answers the sub-question that whiten.py's own docstring flags as the only real design decision.

STAGE B - honest utility, confound-controlled (~90 min). MLP with lr swept over {5e-4, 2e-3, 8e-3} (report per-variant best AND spread), 30 epochs; unregularised linear; CNN on true pixels for 'raw' as the ceiling. Also the shared / separate / pool whitening arms.
 DECIDES: question (2)'s cost side. Numbers that matter: paired delta(MLP error) shared-vs-separate, and whether it exceeds the lr-sweep spread. If it does not, separate whitening costs nothing measurable; if it does, it costs exactly that.

STAGE C - overlap-world attack, i.e. \"the attacker holds the exact source images\" (10 min, and it is the highest-value 10 min in the study). Norm shortlist + anchor-distance verification -> matched pairs -> Procrustes for A_hat -> apply to UNMATCHED rows -> smuggled CNN. Sweep anchors {50, 200, 1000}; run the matched-knowledge and adaptive-scale arms of the fit-set question.
 DECIDES: question (3) in the overlap world, and whether the hold-out draw is optional. Numbers that matter: ||A_hat - A||/||A||, pixel rel-RMS on unmatched rows, smuggled-CNN error on unmatched rows, artifact bytes, seconds. Prediction to falsify: <1 s, <2 KB, error within 1 point of the CNN-on-true-pixels ceiling, for EVERY variant. If that holds, no choice of W or Q matters in the overlap world and the entire defence reduces to \"the draw must be held out\" - which reframes the organizer's question and saves the rest of the budget.

STAGE D - informed attack, held-out world (~3 h). x_pub = the disjoint 40k (already what common.draw gives); additionally repeat the 3 headline cells on a genuinely different 9x9 source (KMNIST or EMNIST-digits, area-resized with the same _area_weights) so \"informed but not overlapping\" is real and not an artifact of same-distribution rows. Inits: eig, cls, 5 random restarts, plus perturbed-truth warm starts at 5/15/45 degrees. Metrics: loss_at_truth vs final_loss; active-pixel matched energy; pixel rel-RMS; SMUGGLED-CNN ERROR; artifact bytes at 0.5 / 2 / 20 KB quantisation; seconds.
 DECIDES: question (1). The value of whitening is exactly the gap between the 'eig'-init result on 'rot' (spectrum preserved, should succeed) and on 'zca+rot' (spectrum destroyed, should fail), measured as smuggled-CNN error. If the 'cls' init plus refinement closes that gap on both, whitening buys nothing and rotation alone is neither enough nor insufficient - the release map is simply not the defence. The warm-start control is what licenses any negative conclusion.

STAGE E - blind attack, screened (~90 min). Only 'rot' (as the equivalence check from Stage 0) and 'zca_1e-3+rot' and 'pca60+rot'. One unmixer (FastICA logcosh) plus sparse_nonneg only on cells where FastICA's localisation exceeds the random-rotation null. Feeds: abs-pcorr and pos-pcorr, with raw-corr once per variant as the null. QAP budget as a CURVE at {2, 10, 30, 120} s, not a single point. End-to-end: smuggled CNN on the attacker's arranged images, fresh in-competition CNN on the recovered layout, honest MLP on released features, and the ORACLE-LAYOUT fresh CNN as the control.
 DECIDES: question (3) in the blind world. The number that decides it is the gap between the fresh-CNN-on-recovered-layout error and the honest-MLP error, at a QAP budget the scored submission could actually afford (the 2 s and 10 s points, not 120 s). If the attack only wins at 120 s and the honest MLP fits in 30 s, the attack is self-defeating under the energy ranking and the defence holds for economic, not cryptographic, reasons - which is a perfectly good answer and should be stated as such.

STAGE F - attack the separate-fit release (30 min). Re-run Stages C and D against zca_1e-3+rot_separate.
 DECIDES: question (2)'s benefit side. If attack success is statistically unchanged from the shared release, separate whitening is pure cost and the recommendation is one shared map.

SUMMARY TABLE THAT ANSWERS THE THREE QUESTIONS (one row per variant): [honest MLP error, best lr] | [dead-subspace principal angle] | [overlap-world smuggled-CNN error, bytes, seconds] | [held-out informed smuggled-CNN error, loss gap vs truth] | [blind fresh-CNN error at 10 s QAP vs honest MLP error] | [max-over-Q of each attack number]. Question (1) is read off the informed column's rot-vs-whitened difference; question (2) off Stage B's cost paired with Stage F's (predicted null) benefit; question (3) off the overlap and held-out smuggled-CNN columns, with the bytes column saying whether the attack is even shippable under the 20 KB cap.

synthesis.predictions:
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTIONS (written before the runs; each is falsifiable, with the number that would falsify it). Calibration probes already run on this machine are cited where they pin a prediction.

P-A1 (fixed-map fold-in). With the current code (common.release derives Q from `seed*7919+17`, W from a public recipe on a public fit set), an int8-quantised A_inv of 6,723 bytes reconstructs held-out pixels at rel-RMS < 0.01 on active pixels, and the offline CNN on that reconstruction lands within 0.3 pp of the same CNN on true pixels, in < 1 ms of submission time. With a per-evaluation fresh rotation_seed the SAME blob drops the CNN to >= 85% error (chance-ish). FALSIFIED IF int8 reconstruction rel-RMS > 0.05 or the CNN gap exceeds 1 pp.

P-A2 (self-whitening equivalence). After attacker self-whitening, the clouds from `rot` and from `zca_eps0+rot` at the same draw+rotation seed align under orthogonal Procrustes to Frobenius residual < 1e-5 relative, and every blind metric (matched energy, edge precision, end-to-end CNN error) agrees between the two arms within Monte-Carlo error over 5 rotation seeds (paired |delta edge-precision| < 0.03, TOST at that margin). eps=1e-3 and eps=1e-2 will NOT match (the tail is not white); predicted paired delta in the eps>0 arms is driven entirely by the tail directions. FALSIFIED IF rot vs zca_eps0+rot differ by more than the 0.03 margin on any blind metric.

P-A3 (zero-atom facet recovery, the top blind attack). Contrast = soft mass of samples within h of the projection's minimum, NOT the (mean-min)/std ratio. Measured here: true pixel directions have atom mass 0.046-0.9998 (median 0.71) while 500 random and 500 non-negative-mixture directions max out at 1.5e-4 -- a ~1000x margin; and a 192-restart search on the RATIO objective reached the true-pixel ratio value (0.541) while recovering zero pixel axes (best |cos| 0.54). PREDICTION: the atom-mass search recovers >= 40 of the 81 pixel axes at |cos| > 0.9 on `zca1e-3+rot` and on `pca60+rot`, blind, in < 120 s CPU / < 5 s GPU, with zero smuggled bytes; the recovered set is strongly biased to the 48 pixels with zero-fraction > 0.5 and misses most of the ~10 densest interior cells. Downstream: topology.recover_layout on the recovered coordinates gives edge-precision@1.0 >= 0.8 (chance ~0.09), and the offline CNN on the completed pixel estimate lands within 3 pp of pixel-space. FALSIFIED IF < 15 axes at |cos| > 0.9, or if edge precision stays below 0.3.
P-A3b (countermeasure pricing). Dither x by U(0, 1/255) before the map collapses the atom-mass margin to < 10x and the recovery to < 10 axes, at an honest-MLP cost of < 0.2 pp. PCA truncation to k=60 leaves a thin slab rather than a point atom: predicted partial survival, 15-40 axes.

P-A4 (rotation-only informed eigen-match). On `rot` with 20k released rows, closed-form Q_hat = V_z S V_x^T with skewness sign fixing gives per-direction |cos| > 0.95 for the top 40 eigendirections (measured relative gaps of the pool covariance: top-20 gaps 37%, 14%, 7.1%, 7.6%, 24%, 21%, 18%, 5.8%, 9.1%, 23%, only two below 3%, against a 1.0% sampling floor at n=20k), pixel rel-RMS < 0.1 on active pixels, and offline-CNN error within 0.5 pp of pixel-space, in < 10 ms with a 6.7 KB int8 artifact. On any exactly-white arm (`zca_eps0+rot`, `pca60+rot`) the identical code returns chance (matched energy ~1/81 = 0.012). THAT GAP IS THE ENTIRE MEASURED VALUE OF WHITENING. FALSIFIED IF the rot arm fails to beat 0.5 mean matched energy, or if the whitened arm beats 0.05.

P-A5 (class-conditional covariance Procrustes). 10 class covariances = 33,210 equations for 3,240 unknowns, but each is estimated from ~1,000 rows (28% relative operator-norm error). PREDICTION: with the class-mean Procrustes init plus >= 5 restarts and LBFGS polish, final_loss reaches within 1.15x of loss_at_truth, giving mean active-pixel matched energy 0.35-0.7, pixel rel-RMS 0.3-0.6, and smuggled-CNN error within 3-8 pp of pixel-space -- a partial break that a nuisance-augmented CNN (P-A12) converts into a near-complete one. Identical metrics (within 0.05 matched energy) on `rot` and on every whitened arm, per P-A2. Success degrades by less than 0.1 matched energy when the class covariances are compressed to rank-12 int8 (9.7 KB). On the held-out KMNIST/EMNIST draw, matched energy drops by >= 0.2. FALSIFIED IF final_loss is more than 2x loss_at_truth on a majority of the 15 cells (which would mean the optimiser, not the defence, is what was measured) or if matched energy exceeds 0.9 (a complete break, which changes the recommendation).

P-A6 (class-mean anchor, 810 bytes). Standalone: exactly 9 recovered directions, |cos| > 0.99 on the between-class subspace, rank-9 reconstruction, smuggled-CNN error > 30% (near-failure). As an initialiser it raises A5's rate of reaching within 1.15x of loss_at_truth from < 50% of random-init restarts to > 90%. FALSIFIED IF the init makes no difference to A5's success rate over 15 cells.

P-A7 (exact-source norm match then Procrustes). Already measured at the label-lookup stage: 99.93-99.98% label accuracy for every variant when the attacker refits W on the same public pool the organiser used (results/exact-*.json). PREDICTION for the continuation: 200 norm-matched anchor rows suffice to recover A by least squares to ||A_hat - A||/||A|| < 0.02, after which pixel rel-RMS on UNMATCHED rows is < 0.05 and the offline CNN on those rows is within 1 pp of pixel-space -- for all variants, in < 1 s, with an artifact under 2 KB (norm table only). Overlap sweep: Procrustes still recovers A at < 0.1 relative error with as few as 200 matched rows, i.e. 2% draw overlap; below ~100 anchors it degrades sharply. The existing 15.5%/16.0% "train-fit" numbers are an artefact of the attacker guessing the wrong fit set, not a property of the variant: a matched-knowledge attacker (refits W on the same rows) or an adaptive attacker (estimates the per-direction scaling from Cov(z_train)) returns to > 99%. FALSIFIED IF the matched-knowledge arm stays below 90%.

P-A8 (frozen CNN + learned linear adapter, no basis recovery). Structural claim: {f(Mz+b)} contains f(x) exactly for every invertible release. PREDICTION: a Stiefel-parameterised adapter (3,240 free params) in front of a frozen offline CNN, trained on the 10k released labels with a non-negativity penalty on the reconstruction, reaches within 1.5 pp of the offline CNN's pixel-space error on EVERY variant including pca60+rot and the separate-whitening arm, in 1-3 s CPU-equivalent, with a 3-8 KB int8 artifact. The unconstrained 6,561-parameter adapter is 0.5-2 pp worse (overfits 10k labels). The decisive comparison is against the honest MLP on released features, NOT against chance. FALSIFIED IF the Stiefel adapter loses more than 4 pp to pixel-space on any variant, which would mean linear obfuscation does impose a real price.

P-A9 (eps-floor tail leak). Measured: the six smallest pool eigenvalues are 1.51e-8, 3.10e-8, 2.11e-7, 3.11e-7, 3.85e-7, 4.07e-7 and their eigenvectors are single pixels (peak energy .994, 1.000, .999, .998, .919, .915 -- the four corners plus (0,1) and (1,0)). At eps=1e-3 their released variances are 1.5e-5 ... 4.1e-4, separated from the bulk by ~31x and from each other by factors 2.05/6.79/1.48/1.24/1.06 against a 1.4% sampling floor at n=20k. PREDICTION: one eigh of Cov(z) recovers >= 4 individual corner-pixel axes at |cos| > 0.95 and a 17-dimensional border subspace at principal angle < 5 degrees, blind, zero bytes, < 5 ms -- at eps=1e-2 worse (more directions shrunk), at eps=0 and at pca60 exactly chance (principal angle indistinguishable from a random 17-subspace, ~1/81 matched energy). Honest MLP accuracy differs by < 0.3 pp across eps in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} and pca60. CONSEQUENCE IF CONFIRMED: eps>0 is strictly dominated; ship pca-k truncation with eps=0. FALSIFIED IF eps=0 or pca60 also yields recoverable structure (then the leak is not the floor), or if eps=1e-3 yields none.

P-A10 (blind FastICA, the currently-coded attack -- expected negative). logcosh on 20k rows: mean active-pixel matched energy 0.05-0.25 against the 0.0123 uniform floor and a ZCA ceiling I predict at 0.25-0.45; peak assignment not a bijection; edge precision from the abs-pcorr feed below 0.35 (chance 0.09); end-to-end fresh-CNN-on-recovered-layout error WORSE than the honest MLP on released features. `cube` beats `logcosh` by 0.05-0.15 matched energy. Best-over-8-seeds beats the mean by >= 0.05. This is a negative result about one contrast, not evidence the defence holds; A3 is the blind attack that matters. FALSIFIED IF logcosh edge precision exceeds 0.6.

P-A11 (honest conv-over-dense gap, the gate). At 9x9 with 10,000 training rows, the oracle-layout CNN (shift-augmented) beats the best MLP on raw pixels by 0.5-2.0 pp; the gap on released features is the same by invariance. If the measured gap is < 0.5 pp, the entire smuggling threat is economically dead and the obfuscation layer can be dropped. Fresh-CNN-on-oracle-layout equals CNN-on-true-pixels within 0.3 pp (this is the control that separates "layout recovery failed" from "conv over ICA sources is useless"). FALSIFIED IF the gap exceeds 3 pp (then obfuscation is worth real money) or is negative.

P-A12 (nuisance-augmented smuggled CNN -- the multiplier). A CNN trained offline on ZCA-mixed, dihedrally-augmented, orthogonally-perturbed 9x9 inputs, evaluated on the ORACLE ZCA basis, loses <= 1.0 pp to a clean pixel CNN on true pixels. CONSEQUENCE IF CONFIRMED: control_zca_whitening is the attacker's target, not a safe ceiling, and every partial-recovery attack must be re-scored with this net. FALSIFIED IF the augmented net loses more than 3 pp, in which case "ICA only reaches ZCA" is a genuine defence.

P-A13 (separate vs joint whitening). Honest cost, separate-ZCA vs shared, at n=10,000, paired per draw: MLP loses 0.3-1.5 pp, unregularised linear loses ~0 (it is exactly invariant to a joint map and only mildly hurt by the train/test mismatch), separate-PCA loses > 5 pp with large cross-draw variance. Attacker cost: ZERO -- every attack's success metric on the separate-fit release is within its own seed-to-seed spread of the shared release, and a Sinkhorn/Procrustes cross-split alignment recovers the honest loss to within 0.2 pp in ~1 s. The Wishart-discrepancy "leak" returns chance against a Wishart(I) null. ANSWER: joint. FALSIFIED IF separate whitening measurably reduces any attack's success.

P-A14 (JADE/cumulant and marginal-quantile attacks, label-free informed). Both beat FastICA-logcosh by >= 0.15 matched energy at n=20k and both land in the 0.3-0.6 matched-energy band -- i.e. comparable to A5, not better. Marginal-quantile matching retains >= 60% of its exact-source matched energy on a held-out KMNIST/EMNIST 9x9 draw (zero-inflation and the [0,1] bound transfer); JADE retains >= 40%. This is the pair that decides whether the planned hold-out draw actually helps. FALSIFIED IF either drops below 0.15 matched energy on the same-source draw (attack too weak to inform the hold-out question).
synthesis.protocol:
FINAL EXPERIMENT PROTOCOL. All CPU, on the Intel MacBook (/usr/local/bin/python3.10), zero Modal dollars in the core plan; one optional A100 timing pass at the end costs < $2 of the $10 and uses 1 GPU. Total core wall-clock ~9 h, runnable overnight. Working dir: /Users/yaroslavvb/git/sutro-problems/mnist/experiments/rotation-obfuscation-20260923.

=== P0. STRUCTURAL PREREQUISITES (30 min of edits, zero compute; without them the numbers are uninterpretable) ===
P0.1 Split the seed. common.draw(draw_seed) and the rotation must be independent streams: release(..., draw_seed, rotation_seed). Today Q = haar(dim, seed*7919+17) is locked to the draw, so the variance over Q cannot be estimated at all.
P0.2 Enforce the attacker/scorer boundary mechanically. Attacker entry points take only (z_train, y_train, z_test [, x_pub, y_pub]) and return artifacts; A/W/mu/Q and test labels reach only scoring functions. attacks.py already honours this (`comp = b @ a` is scoring-side); attack_ica.py does not -- its lines 217-219 rescale ICA sources by PIXEL-SPACE synthesis norms taken from the secret A, and line 271 monkeypatches topology.recover_layout globally without restoring it. Delete the attack_ica.py path from this study; keep attacks.py as the single pipeline. Any result already produced through attack_ica.py's rescale is an oracle upper bound and must be relabelled as such.
P0.3 Add the protocol axis w_public in {True, False}, and the artifact axis rotation_fixed in {True, False}. Without these, question (1) is undefined: if W is published (as whiten.py's docstring says it must be), whiten+rotate is a KNOWN map composed with a secret Q, i.e. information-theoretically identical to rotation-only, and the only residual content is the eps tail plus honest utility.
P0.4 Every attack record carries: `bytes` (the quantised offline artifact actually needed), `seconds`, `loss_at_truth` (scoring-side, for any optimised attack), and metrics restricted to ACTIVE pixels (pool variance > 1e-4 -- 64 of 81). common.basis_recovery_report documents "on active pixels only" but never filters; pass the mask and also report the same statistic on the dead columns as a null.

=== VARIANT GRID (8 releases) ===
raw | perm (anchor, 1 seed) | rot | zca_eps0+rot | zca1e-3+rot | zca1e-2+rot | pca60+rot (eps=0, k=60) | zca1e-3+rot_separate (test whitened on its own rows, same Q).
Ablation arms used only where named: dither sigma in {0, 1/255, 0.02} on x before the map; release precision in {float32, round to 1e-3}; w_public in {T,F}; rotation_fixed in {T,F}.

=== SEEDS ===
Security cells: 3 draw_seeds x 5 rotation_seeds = 15 per (variant, attack). Report success FRACTION with a Wilson interval and the MAX over Q (a security claim is about the worst Q an entrant can face, not the mean). Utility cells: 3 draw_seeds x 3 model_seeds, reported as paired per-draw deltas against `raw`, never as absolute accuracies.

=== METRIC SET (every cell, three end-to-end columns + geometry + cost) ===
T2 (the threat to block): offline-trained CNN, frozen, applied to the attacker's PIXEL estimate -> test error.
T2+ : the same with the nuisance-augmented CNN (Stage 6).
T1 (the weaker, arguably legitimate threat): fresh in-competition CNN trained on the recovered layout -> test error.
Honest reference: MLP on released features (per-variant lr-swept), and unregularised linear.
Geometry: active-pixel Hungarian matched energy (+ n>0.5, n>0.9), per-direction |cos| spectrum vs the eigengap / atom-mass covariate, pixel rel-RMS, edge-precision@1.0 with its chance line (0.089) on the same axis as perm's ~0.99.
Cost: attacker seconds and artifact bytes at quantisation levels {0.5 KB, 2 KB, 20 KB}; honest-learner seconds on the same axis. The 20 KB cap is the organiser's real defence, so an attack that does not fit is not an attack.

=== STAGE 0 -- free algebra checks (2 min; if either fails, stop, the pipeline is broken) ===
(a) Unregularised logistic regression (C=1e6 / LBFGS to convergence) must give identical accuracy on raw / rot / zca+rot / pca60+rot for the same draw. The current models.logreg_fit_predict uses C=1.0, whose L2 penalty is basis-dependent -- keep that run only as a separately labelled "regularisation is basis-dependent" demo.
(b) FastICA sources on rot and on zca_eps0+rot at the same draw+rotation must agree to numerical noise (both whiten internally; attacks.sparse_nonneg_unmix also self-ZCAs). This converts the expensive blind rot-vs-whitened comparison from a "result" into a VALIDITY CHECK, and frees the compute for Stage 3.

=== STAGE 1 -- the gate: does the spatial prior buy anything? (60 min) [attacks A11 anchor, A16] ===
Oracle-layout CNN vs best MLP vs unregularised linear on true pixels at n=10,000, 3x3 seeds, with the CNN also run on the ORACLE layout over ICA sources (separating "layout recovery failed" from "conv over sources is useless"). Also the oracle-lattice GNN vs dense MLP as the ceiling for all graph-level attacks.
DECIDES: whether any of the rest matters. If the conv-over-dense gap is < 0.5 pp, stop and report that the obfuscation layer is optional. RUN THIS FIRST.

=== STAGE 2 -- second-order probes, no ICA, no labels, no CNN (15 min) [A9, A4, A2] ===
For each variant x 15 cells: one eigh of Cov(z_all).
2a eps tail leak: principal angles between the bottom-m released eigenvectors and the true dead-pixel subspace; number of individual corner axes at |cos| > 0.9; sweep eps in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2} and k in {60, 70}; pair with honest MLP accuracy at the same setting.
2b rotation-only eigen-Procrustes with skew sign-fixing (informed, disjoint 40k pool), scored end-to-end with the smuggled CNN. Same code run on the whitened arms is the control that must return chance.
2c self-whitening equivalence: Procrustes-align the self-whitened rot and zca_eps0+rot clouds; report the residual, and assert every downstream metric matches (TOST at 0.03 edge precision).
DECIDES: question (1), and the eps-vs-truncation design choice, at negligible cost.

=== STAGE 3 -- blind attacks (3 h) [A3 primary, A14 baseline, A15] ===
3a ZERO-ATOM FACET SEARCH (new, and the top blind attack). CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION NOTE from my calibration probe: use atom MASS, not the (mean-min)/std ratio. The ratio contrast is necessary but not sufficient -- a 192-restart/400-step search minimising it reached the true-pixel value 0.541 while recovering ZERO pixel axes (best |cos| 0.54). Atom mass separates by ~1000x (pixel dirs 0.046-0.9998, random and non-negative-mixture dirs <= 1.5e-4). Objective: maximise sum_i K_h(w.z_i - min_j w.z_j) with a soft-min, 512 restarts batched, repulsion on |cos| between rows, then cluster and deflate. Run on zca1e-3+rot, pca60+rot, zca_eps0+rot, and on the dither arms sigma in {0, 1/255, 0.02} and the rounded-release arm. Hand the recovered coordinates to topology.recover_layout and to the smuggled CNN.
3b FastICA baseline as coded, but: contrast in {logcosh, cube, exp}, 8 seeds, report the BEST (an attacker restarts), check n_iter_ against max_iter to separate "attack failed" from "optimiser failed", and add the energy-correlation feed corr(s_i^2, s_j^2) alongside abs-pcorr / pos-pcorr, with raw-corr kept once per variant as the null. Add a localisation metric that credits localised-but-not-pixel filters (spatial second moment / participation ratio of each composite row reshaped to 9x9) -- ICA returns edge filters, and the peak-energy metric will under-report the threat.
3c sparse-precision / DCT lattice-prior search, rotation-only only; its objective is provably flat after whitening, which is the cleanest statement of what whitening buys blind.
COMPUTE DISCIPLINE: replace topology's single 120 s QAP point with a success-vs-budget CURVE at {2, 10, 30, 120} s, and gate the expensive QAP on a cheap attacker-side screen (mutual-kNN degree / similarity-spectrum gap). A 120 s attack that then trains a CNN may cost more than the honest MLP it is trying to beat -- that is a result the organiser wants, and only the curve can produce it.

=== STAGE 4 -- informed attacks on a DISJOINT pool (3 h) [A5, A6, A11 cumulant, A12 marginal] ===
x_pub = the 40k rows not in the draw (already what common.draw gives). Repeat the 3 headline cells on a genuinely different source (KMNIST or EMNIST-digits area-resized with the same common._area_weights) so "informed but non-overlapping" is real.
Inits: eig, cls (class-mean Procrustes), rlc, 5 random restarts, PLUS perturbed-truth warm starts at 5/15/45 degrees. Report loss_at_truth next to final_loss in every record -- without it, a failed Adam run is indistinguishable from a working defence, and no negative conclusion is licensed.
Attacks: A5 class-conditional covariance Procrustes (the existing informed_attack, repaired); A12 known-marginal/quantile matching on the Stiefel manifold (2.6 KB of 81x32 quantile tables, no independence assumption -- the right contrast for zero-inflated sources); A11 JADE/third-cumulant Procrustes (label-free, the one that matters for the hold-out).
Artifact-size sweep: rank-12 int8 class covariances (9.7 KB), top-k int8 eigenbasis, quantile tables -- report success vs {0.5, 2, 20} KB.

=== STAGE 5 -- the two attacks that ignore the basis entirely (1 h) [A1, A7, A8] ===
5a Fixed-map fold-in: quantise the true A_inv to int8 + per-row float16 scales (6,723 B), apply to a fresh draw, report reconstruction rel-RMS, smuggled-CNN error, exact base64 source size; then repeat with a fresh rotation_seed per evaluation and confirm the blob dies. This is the decision the organiser actually needs.
5b Exact-source continuation: norm shortlist + anchor-distance verification -> matched pairs -> Procrustes for A_hat -> apply to UNMATCHED rows -> smuggled CNN. Sweep anchors {50, 200, 1000} and draw overlap {100%, 10%, 1%, 0.1%}. Add the matched-knowledge arm (attacker refits W on exactly the rows the organiser used) and the adaptive arm (per-direction scale estimated from Cov(z_train)) -- the existing 99.93 vs 15.53 gap in results/exact-zca1e-3+rot-s1.json is a fit-set mismatch artefact, not a property of the variant, and will be misread as "fit W on train and the hole closes".
5c Stiefel-constrained adapter in front of the frozen offline CNN, on every variant including pca60+rot and the separate arm, with the unconstrained 81x81 adapter as the ablation. Scored against the honest MLP at equal wall-clock, not against chance.

=== STAGE 6 -- scoring-side controls (40 min) [A12 multiplier] ===
Nuisance-augmented CNN (ZCA-domain mixing + 8 dihedrals + small orthogonal perturbations in near-degenerate subspaces) evaluated on the ORACLE ZCA basis, against the clean pixel CNN. One number; it decides whether "the attack only reached the ZCA basis" is a defence or a formality, and every partial-recovery attack in Stages 3-4 is re-scored with it.

=== STAGE 7 -- separate vs joint whitening, both sides (45 min) [A13, A17] ===
Honest cost: shared / separate-W-shared-Q / separate-PCA / pool-fit x {unregularised linear, MLP with lr swept over 5e-4, 2e-3, 8e-3, conv} x 3x3 seeds, reported as paired per-draw deltas, with the lr-sweep SPREAD printed next to the variant effect (if the spread exceeds the effect, say so -- the current fixed lr=2e-3 confounds conditioning with the release map).
Attacker side (currently missing entirely): re-run Stage 4 and Stage 5b against the separate-fit release, plus the attacker's cross-split Sinkhorn/Procrustes repair, plus the fold-bootstrap Wishart-anisotropy probe against a Wishart(I) null.
DECIDES: question (2) on both the cost and the benefit side.

=== STAGE 8 (OPTIONAL, <= $2, 1 GPU, 15 min A100) ===
Time and energy for the 6 surviving (release, submission) pairs, so the ranking axis is in real joules: honest MLP, honest conv, atom-facet attack + CNN, adapter + frozen CNN, informed Procrustes + CNN, norm-match + CNN. Everything else in this study is 81-dimensional and belongs on the CPU.

=== SUMMARY TABLE THAT ANSWERS THE THREE QUESTIONS (one row per variant) ===
[honest MLP error, best lr, lr spread] | [dead-subspace principal angle, corner axes recovered] | [blind atom-facet: axes recovered, edge precision, T2 error, seconds, bytes] | [blind FastICA best-of-8: matched energy, T1 error vs honest MLP] | [informed disjoint-pool: matched energy, final/at-truth loss ratio, T2 and T2+ error, bytes] | [adapter+frozen CNN error] | [exact-source: T2 error on unmatched rows, overlap threshold] | [max-over-Q of every attack column].
Question (1) is read off the Stage-2 rot-vs-whitened gap in the informed column. Question (2) off Stage 7's cost paired with its (predicted null) benefit. Question (3) off the T2/T2+ columns for blind and informed, with the bytes column saying whether the attack is even shippable under 20 KB.
synthesis.defence_notes:
WHAT THE MERGED RED TEAM AGREES ON, AND WHAT I MEASURED TODAY.

All three red teams converge on one structural point, and my probes support it: the attacker can always whiten the released cloud himself, so for every variant the residual secret is the same object -- one unknown element of O(d) acting on the canonically whitened data. Whitening on the organiser's side deletes exactly the unconditional covariance (3,321 equations) out of roughly 1.9M identifying equations available to an informed attacker (class means 810, class-conditional covariances 33,210, third cumulants ~88k, fourth ~1.8M). It removes the cheapest and most robust channel -- which is worth doing -- and nothing else. ZCA vs PCA is a non-choice once Q is Haar (whiten.py already proves Q W_zca = (QU) W_pca with QU Haar); the only real knobs are eps, k, and dither.

ANSWER TO Q1 (is rotation alone enough?). No. Rotation-only releases Cov(z) = Q Sigma Q^T and an informed attacker inverts it with one eigendecomposition plus 81 skewness sign bits; the pool's top-20 relative eigengaps, which I measured, are 37%, 14%, 7.1%, 7.6%, 24%, 21%, 18%, 5.8%, 9.1%, 23% with only two below 3%, against a 1.0% sampling floor at n=20k, so the recovery is essentially exact and costs milliseconds. Whitening is NECESSARY. It is not sufficient, and the gap between the eig-init attack on `rot` and on `zca_eps0+rot` is the entire measured value of whitening -- report that one number.

ANSWER TO Q2 (separate or joint?). Joint, unambiguously, and this is the one question I would answer before running anything. Separate whitening buys no obfuscation (the attacker self-whitens each split regardless), costs honest accuracy through a train/test map mismatch of order sqrt(d/n) = sqrt(81/10000) ~ 9% in the covariance, is partly undoable by the honest learner re-whitening both splits, and -- the perverse part -- pushes honest entrants to estimate the cross-split alignment over O(81), which is literally the attacker's machinery. Separate PCA is worse than dominated: split-half PCA eigenvectors at n=10,000 are unstable (red team 3 measured several top-40 overlaps at 0.65-0.69, i.e. 40-50 degree rotations, plus arbitrary sign flips), so separate-PCA is a broken task rather than a defence variant. Fit one shared map on the pool or on the union of released train+test rows.

ANSWER TO Q3 (can the attacker still get the pixel basis?). Very likely yes, and I found the sharpest blind route today. Non-negativity plus exact-zero atoms is the structure that no invertible linear map can hide: a 9x9 area-resized pixel is exactly zero in 4.4% to 99.99% of images (48 of 81 pixels in more than half), so each pixel is a supporting facet touched by thousands of released points. My measurement: on the zca1e-3+rot release, true pixel directions carry atom mass 0.046-0.9998 (median 0.71) while 500 random directions and 500 non-negative-mixture directions top out at 1.5e-4 -- a ~1000x margin, invisible to every moment-based statistic and untouched by whitening or the eps floor. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to red team 3's version: the scale-invariant RATIO contrast (mean-min)/std is necessary but NOT sufficient. I ran a 192-restart, 400-step search on the ratio; it reached 0.541, exactly the true-pixel value, while recovering zero pixel axes (best |cos| to any pixel axis 0.54, none above 0.9). Any non-negative mixture sits on the cone boundary too. The contrast that actually identifies facets is atom MASS. Build the attack that way or it will produce a false negative and the study will conclude the defence holds.

THE HOLE THAT DOMINATES ALL THE CRYPTANALYSIS. common.release derives Q deterministically from the draw seed (`seed*7919+17`) and whiten.py fits W, mu on the fixed 60k pool with a single DEFAULT_ROTATION_SEED, describing the map as a protocol constant that must be published. If A is a constant across draws and submissions, none of these attacks are needed: an int8 A_inv with per-row float16 scales is 6,723 bytes, ~9 KB base64, comfortably inside a 20 KB cap, and it is the exact analogue of the 1.8 KB table that already undoes the pixel permutation. The defence's security level is then "one determined entrant, once". Fresh (mu, W, Q) per scored evaluation, with no dev/practice phase sharing the final Q, is the change that has to land before E1-E4 mean anything -- and it is also where the real margin lives, because it forces the 3,240-parameter recovery to happen inside the scored window every time.

THE SIZE CAP IS NOT A DEFENCE AGAINST SPATIAL-FEATURE SMUGGLING. An 8-filter 3x3 edge bank is 72 numbers; a usable int8 9x9 CNN is 3-8 KB; the informed artifacts all fit (eigenbasis 6.7 KB, per-pixel quantiles 2.6 KB, rank-12 class covariances 9.7 KB). The cap only stops smuggling a large model. It does bite in exactly two places worth measuring: full class covariances (33 KB) and a stored reference cloud for OT-based alignment (>100 KB).

DESIGN LEVERS, IN ORDER OF COST-EFFECTIVENESS.
(i) Fresh secret (mu, W, Q) per scored evaluation. Closes the amortised-crack hole; everything else is downstream of this.
(ii) A genuinely held-out draw with zero overlap with anything derivable from public 9x9 data. Pairwise distances and norms are exact O(d) invariants, so no choice of W, eps or k touches the sample-matching channel -- only novelty does. The overlap sweep in Stage 5b tells you how clean "zero overlap" has to be; my prediction is that 1-2% overlap already suffices for Procrustes to recover the whole map, not merely the matched labels.
(iii) PCA truncation with eps=0 instead of a variance floor. Measured: the six smallest pool eigenvalues are 1.51e-8 ... 4.07e-7 and their eigenvectors ARE single pixels (peak energy .994, 1.000, .999, .998, .919, .915 -- the four corners and two edge cells). At eps=1e-3 those become released variances 1.5e-5 ... 4.1e-4, separated from the bulk by ~31x, so one eigh hands a blind attacker four exact corner axes plus a 17-dimensional border subspace -- and the corners are precisely what resolves the dihedral ambiguity that topology.py says no unlabelled statistic can break. Note attack_ica.py's main() defaults to epsilon=1e-2, the leakiest setting.
(iv) Small dither on x before the map, U(0, 1/255) or Gaussian sigma ~0.02. It adds no rotational security (isotropic noise is Q-equivariant) but it annihilates the exact-zero atoms that the strongest blind attack depends on, and caps the precision of every moment-matching attack. Price it against honest accuracy in Stage 3a -- my prediction is under 0.2 pp, which would make it the best value in the list after (i) and (ii).
(v) Accept that a labelled linear adapter in front of a frozen smuggled CNN is invariant to EVERY invertible linear release, by construction, and defend that case on the evaluation side (ranked hold-out, per-draw secrets, energy accounting that charges for the adapter's training) rather than by obfuscation.

MEASUREMENT HAZARDS THAT WOULD PRODUCE A WRONG CONCLUSION.
(a) attack_ica.py:217-219 rescales ICA sources by their PIXEL-SPACE synthesis norms, computed from the secret A, and the comment says that rescale is load-bearing for the downstream topology attack. That is an oracle attacker. Delete the path or relabel every number from it as an upper bound.
(b) attack_ica.py:271 monkeypatches topology.recover_layout globally and never restores it, so later cells in the same process silently reuse a stale layout.
(c) mean_peak_energy_fraction is the wrong headline. ICA on digit images converges to localised edge filters, not pixels, so it will read as reassuringly low while the attack has already succeeded for the attacker's purpose. Report end-to-end T2 error as the headline and add a localisation metric that credits localised-but-not-pixel filters.
(d) A failed optimiser is not a defence. informed_attack fits 3,240 Stiefel parameters with 600 Adam steps from at most three inits and never reports the loss at the TRUE R. Add loss_at_truth, 5 restarts, and perturbed-truth warm starts; a negative result is only licensed if the optimiser can stay at the truth when started there.
(e) Adjacency metrics must be anchored to ground truth, not to the attack's own peak assignment, and restricted to the 64 active pixels; the ~17 dead border cells are free columns in the Hungarian assignment and inflate matched energy by an unknown amount.
(f) Every "we found structure" statistic needs a Wishart(I) / random-rotation null run through the identical pipeline.
(g) Score the two threats in separate columns throughout. T1 = recover any locally-structured basis and train a conv net in-competition (easy, arguably legitimate). T2 = recover pixels up to a dihedral and apply frozen offline weights (hard, the actual thing to block). Every localisation metric currently in the harness measures T2 only, and a defence that blocks T2 while leaving T1 open is fine if the honest conv-over-dense gap is small -- which is why Stage 1 runs first.

IF STAGE 1 RETURNS A GAP UNDER ~0.5 pp, the honest recommendation is to drop the obfuscation layer entirely and rely on the two defences already known to work -- a genuinely held-out draw plus the source-size cap -- and to spend the remaining budget on the hold-out design instead.

ranked_attacks.name: Fixed-map fold-in: smuggle A_inv (or the composed first layer) instead of attacking
ranked_attacks.target: all variants (rot, zca+rot any eps, pca-k, separate)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: If (mu, W, Q) are a protocol constant -- which is what whiten.py's docstring says and what common.release's seed-derived Q implements -- then no attack is needed. Crack A once offline with unlimited compute, ship A_inv as 81x81 int8 with 81 per-row float16 scales (6,723 B, ~9 KB base64), and reconstruct pixels in one GEMM. Or fold A_inv into the frozen CNN's first layer: h = W1 x + b1 becomes h = (W1 A_inv) z + (b1 + W1 mu), so the artifact is only as large as the first layer.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: Ainv = np.linalg.inv(A); scale = np.abs(Ainv).max(1)/127; q8 = np.round(Ainv/scale[:,None]).astype(np.int8)  # 6561 B + 162 B\n# in submission: x = z @ (q8*scale[:,None]).T + mu ; logits = smuggled_cnn(x.reshape(-1,1,9,9))\n# then repeat with a FRESH rotation_seed per evaluation and confirm the blob dies (this is the decision)
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Full pixel recovery at ~0 submission cost; reconstruction rel-RMS < 0.01, smuggled-CNN within 0.3 pp of pixel-space. Dominates every other attack and makes rotation and whitening decorative. Dies completely under per-evaluation fresh (mu, W, Q).
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: < 1 ms submission (one 81x81 GEMM); 6.7 KB artifact; 5 min to measure.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 1,2,3 (it voids all three unless per-evaluation secrets are adopted)

ranked_attacks.name: Exact-source norm match, then Procrustes recovery of the whole map
ranked_attacks.mechanism: ||z|| = ||W(x-mu)|| is an exact O(d) invariant and W is attacker-recomputable from the published recipe, so released rows can be matched to public images by norm (disambiguated by distances to a few identified anchors). The organiser already knows the label-lookup version; the damaging continuation is that ~200 matched pairs give A by least squares/Procrustes, after which EVERY row -- including unmatched rows and the whole test set -- is in the true pixel gauge.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
nz = norm(z_test,axis=1); shortlist by searchsorted against a smuggled norm table; verify with distances to 20 anchors
A_hat = lstsq(X_matched - mu, Z_matched)   # or Procrustes after self-whitening
X_all = (z_all - offset) @ pinv(A_hat).T ; pred = smuggled_cnn(X_all[unmatched])
# sweep anchors {50,200,1000} x overlap {100%,10%,1%,0.1%}; add matched-knowledge and adaptive-scale arms
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: ||A_hat-A||/||A|| < 0.02 from 200 anchors; pixel rel-RMS < 0.05 on unmatched rows; CNN within 1 pp of pixel-space; < 1 s, < 2 KB. The existing 99.93-vs-15.53 split in results/exact-zca1e-3+rot-s1.json is a fit-set-guess artefact and will be misread unless the matched-knowledge arm is run.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: < 1 s; artifact 1-2 KB (norm table) up to 16 KB (200 int4 reference images); 10 min to measure.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (and whether the hold-out draw is optional or mandatory)

ranked_attacks.name: Frozen offline CNN plus a learned linear adapter (no basis recovery at all)
ranked_attacks.target: all variants incl. pca-k and separate whitening
ranked_attacks.attacker: either (informed for the CNN, blind for the fit)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: For any frozen nonlinear f trained offline in pixel space, the class {f(Mz+b): M in GL(d)} contains f(x) exactly, since M = A_inv, b = mu is in the class. So the release charges the attacker only the cost of estimating the adapter from the 10k released labels. Constraining M = W^{-1} Q^T with Q on the Stiefel manifold (when W is published) cuts the free parameters from 6,561 to 3,240. A non-negativity penalty on the reconstruction supplies free extra signal.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: Q = Parameter(eye(81)); for ep in range(40): Qo,_ = qr(Q); xb = (zb @ Qo) @ inv(W).T + mu\n  loss = CE(frozen_cnn(xb.view(-1,1,9,9)), yb) + 0.1*relu(-xb).pow(2).mean()\n# ablations: unconstrained 81x81 adapter; random vs attack-derived init; n in {1k,3.2k,10k}
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Within 1.5 pp of pixel-space on every variant, in 1-3 s, with a 3-8 KB int8 CNN. This is the structural reason no invertible linear release can stop spatial-feature smuggling; if it lands, the decision moves entirely to evaluation-side controls.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 1-3 s CPU-equivalent per cell; 3-8 KB artifact; ~45 min for the full grid.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (and reframes 1 and 2 as irrelevant if it succeeds)

ranked_attacks.name: Rotation-only: informed eigen-Procrustes with third-moment sign fixing
ranked_attacks.target: rot (control: every whitened arm, where it must return chance)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Cov(z) = Q Sigma Q^T, so Q = V_z S V_x^T with S an unknown sign diagonal fixed by comparing per-direction skewness against the offline table. Measured pool eigengaps (top-20: 37, 14, 7.1, 7.6, 24, 21, 18, 5.8, 9.1, 23 %) sit far above the 1.0% sampling floor at n=20k, so the top ~40 directions are recovered essentially exactly.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: dz,Vz = eigh(cov(z)); dx,Vx = eigh(Sigma_pub)\nS = sign(skew(z@Vz) * skew_pub); Qhat = (Vz*S) @ Vx.T; xhat = z @ Qhat + mu_pub\n# report per-direction |cos| vs relative eigengap; sweep N in {1k,3k,10k,20k}; run identical code on zca_eps0+rot as the null
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: |cos| > 0.95 on the top 40 directions, rel-RMS < 0.1, CNN within 0.5 pp of pixel-space; chance on any exactly-white arm. The rot-vs-white gap IS the measured value of whitening.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: < 10 ms; 6.7 KB int8 eigenbasis (2.5 KB for top-30); 10 min total.

ranked_attacks.name: Zero-atom facet recovery (non-negative cone, Plumbley NNICA) -- ATOM MASS, not the ratio contrast
ranked_attacks.target: all variants; killed by dither, partly by truncation
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Every pixel is exactly zero in a large fraction of images (measured: min 4.36%, 48/81 above 50%, 79/81 above 5%), so {x_p=0} maps to a hyperplane carrying thousands of released points: the cloud lives in a cone whose facets are the pixel axes. This is an ORDER property, preserved by every invertible linear map, and untouched by whitening, the eps floor or PCA truncation.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
# CALIBRATED CORRECTION: maximise atom MASS, not (mean-min)/std.
# probe result: ratio search (192 restarts x 400 steps) hit the true-pixel ratio 0.541 with best |cos| 0.54 and 0/192 axes recovered.
# atom mass separates by ~1000x: pixel dirs 0.046-0.9998 (median 0.71) vs random and nonneg-mixture dirs <= 1.5e-4.
P = Zw @ Wn.T; t = softmin(P, tau); J = exp(-((P-t)**2)/h**2).mean(0)
maximise J.sum() - lam*repulsion(Wn) over 512 batched restarts; cluster by |cos|>0.98; deflate; keep 81 clusters
then topology.recover_layout on the recovered coordinates -> smuggled CNN
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: 40-70 of 81 axes at |cos| > 0.9 (biased to the 48 high-zero-fraction cells, missing the densest interior), edge precision >= 0.8 against a 0.089 chance line, CNN within 3 pp of pixel-space. Dither U(0,1/255) should collapse it to < 10 axes at < 0.2 pp honest cost -- that ablation is the cheapest real countermeasure in the study.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~43 s measured for 192 restarts x 400 steps on 4 CPU threads; ~5 s on an A100; zero offline bytes (plus 1.8 KB permutation table + CNN downstream).
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (the blind half, and it is the attack that survives any hold-out draw)

ranked_attacks.name: Class-conditional covariance Procrustes / joint diagonalisation
ranked_attacks.target: whiten+rotate (and identically rot, per the self-whitening lemma)
ranked_attacks.attacker: informed, disjoint pool, uses the 10k released labels
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Whitening sterilises only the MARGINAL covariance. Cov(z|c) = Q B_c Q^T with B_c computable offline: 10 x 3,321 equations for 3,240 unknowns, second-order only (no non-Gaussianity needed), degenerate only where all ten class covariances are simultaneously isotropic. Solve on the Stiefel manifold from the class-mean init. Already implemented as attacks.informed_attack; needs loss_at_truth, restarts and warm starts to be interpretable.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: A_c = [cov(zw[y==c]) for c in range(10)]; B_c = rank-12 int8 smuggled factors\nR = procrustes(class_means) ; 500 Stiefel steps on sum_c ||R B_c R^T - A_c||_F^2 + 4*mean terms ; LBFGS polish\nREQUIRED: report loss_at_truth (scoring-side) next to final_loss; >=5 random restarts; warm starts at truth+{5,15,45} degrees
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: final_loss within 1.15x of loss_at_truth; matched energy 0.35-0.7; rel-RMS 0.3-0.6; CNN within 3-8 pp of pixel-space -- a partial break that the nuisance-augmented CNN converts into a near-complete one. Drops >= 0.2 matched energy on a held-out different-source draw.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~100-300 ms per restart; 9.7 KB rank-12 int8 artifact (full B_c is 33 KB, over cap -- the cap genuinely bites here); ~2 h for the full grid with restarts.
