ranked_attacks.name: eps variance-floor tail leak (corner-pixel axes from one eigendecomposition)
ranked_attacks.target: zca1e-3+rot, zca1e-2+rot; control: eps=0 and pca60
ranked_attacks.attacker: blind (informed version also names the pixels)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: With a floor, Cov(z) = Q diag(lam/(lam+eps)) Q^T is not the identity, so its eigenvectors are identified wherever the shrinkage factors differ. Measured: the six smallest pool eigenvalues are 1.51e-8, 3.10e-8, 2.11e-7, 3.11e-7, 3.85e-7, 4.07e-7 and their eigenvectors ARE single pixels (peak energy .994, 1.000, .999, .998, .919, .915 -- corners (0,0),(8,0),(8,8),(0,8) plus (0,1),(1,0)); at eps=1e-3 their released variances are 1.5e-5...4.1e-4, separated from the bulk by ~31x against a 1.4% sampling floor.

Standalone smuggling value ~0 (these pixels carry no information) but it breaks the dihedral ambiguity topology.py cannot break and shrinks the Stiefel search from SO(81) to SO(64).
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: < 5 ms per cell, zero bytes; 15 min for the whole sweep including the honest-accuracy pairing.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 1 (the eps-vs-truncation design choice inside the whitening arm)

ranked_attacks.name: Honest conv-over-dense gap and the locality-without-identity threat (T1)
ranked_attacks.target: n/a -- the gate that decides whether any defence is worth building
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Two threats are being conflated. T2 (smuggling) needs pixels up to a dihedral; T1 needs only ANY basis with usable 2-D neighbourhood structure, then trains a conv learner in-competition -- no offline artifact, no alignment. The decisive quantity is the accuracy gap between a conv learner on the oracle layout and the best dense learner on released features at n=10,000. If that gap is small, the whole obfuscation design is optional.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: err_mlp = mlp_fit_predict(z_train,y,z_test); err_conv_true = cnn_fit_predict(x_train,y,x_test)\nerr_conv_oracle_layout = cnn on ICA sources arranged by the TRUE peak-pixel layout (separates layout failure from 'conv over sources is useless')\nalso: oracle-lattice GNN vs dense MLP (upper bound for every graph-level attack)
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Predicted gap 0.5-2.0 pp at 9x9 with 10k rows. Under 0.5 pp means smuggling buys almost nothing and the recommendation becomes 'hold-out draw + size cap, drop the obfuscation'.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~60 min CPU for 3x3 seeds including the oracle controls.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 1,2,3 (it is the gate; run it before everything else)

ranked_attacks.name: Self-whitening reduction lemma (validity check, not an attack)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: z_hat = Cov(z)^{-1/2}(z - zbar) equals R Sigma^{-1/2}(x-mu) for some orthogonal R, for EVERY choice of W. So rotation-only, ZCA+eps, PCA+eps and rank-k truncation deliver the same object up to an unknown element of O(d). Any measured gap between them AFTER attacker self-whitening is a bug or a conditioning artefact, not security. This must be applied before every other attack and it predicts the whole E1/E2 result structure.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
C = cov(z); d,V = eigh(C); Whalf = (V/sqrt(clip(d,1e-12))) @ V.T; zw = (z - z.mean(0)) @ Whalf.T
assert allclose(cov(zw), eye(d), atol=1e-6)
# Procrustes-align the self-whitened rot and zca_eps0+rot clouds at the same draw+rotation; report the residual
# then TOST every downstream metric at a 0.03 edge-precision margin
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Residual < 1e-5 relative for eps=0; every blind metric statistically identical between rot and zca_eps0+rot. eps>0 arms will NOT match, and the difference localises entirely in the tail -- which is the eps leak, measured a second way.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: < 1 ms per cell; 5 min total. Frees the compute otherwise wasted running the blind stage twice.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 1 (it is what makes the rot-vs-white comparison interpretable)

ranked_attacks.name: Separate train/test whitening: honest cost plus the attacker's free repair
ranked_attacks.target: zca1e-3+rot_separate, and separate-PCA as the cautionary arm
ranked_attacks.mechanism: With per-split W the composite mismatch is Q W_te W_tr^{-1} Q^T = Q(I+E)Q^T with E the sampling difference of two covariance estimates at n=10,000, d=81 -- relative spectral error ~sqrt(d/n) = 9%. That is a pure covariate shift on the honest learner and worth nothing defensively: the attacker self-whitens each split independently, so his pipeline is unchanged, and he can align the two splits by Sinkhorn/Procrustes in ~1 s. Per-split Q is worse: the honest task then requires the attacker's own rotation-alignment machinery.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
for mode in ('joint','separate_W','separate_Q'): err[mode] = fit_predict(release(mode), family) for family in (unreg-linear, MLP-lr-swept, conv)
# attacker repair: R = sinkhorn_procrustes(selfwhiten(z_te), selfwhiten(z_tr)); err_repaired ?= err['joint']
# leak null: fold-bootstrap covariance anisotropy vs a Wishart(I) null run through the identical pipeline
# ALSO re-run the informed and norm-match attacks against the separate release (currently never done)
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: MLP loses 0.3-1.5 pp for separate-ZCA, ~0 for unregularised linear, > 5 pp with large cross-draw variance for separate-PCA; attacker success unchanged within seed spread; the Wishart leak returns chance. Answer: joint.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~45 min CPU including the lr sweep and the attacker re-runs.

ranked_attacks.name: Blind FastICA (logcosh / cube / exp) -> topology -> CNN, as currently coded
ranked_attacks.mechanism: The existing attacks.fastica + topology pipeline. Expected to underperform for three separable reasons: contrast mismatch (logcosh targets symmetric heavy tails, 9x9 pixels are one-sided and zero-inflated), target mismatch (the maximally-independent basis of image-like data is localised edge filters, not pixels, so the peak-energy ceiling is the ZCA control), and sample size at the margin (5d^2 = 33k vs 20k rows). Must be run anyway: it is the first thing any entrant tries and the contrast ablation is cheap.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
for fun in ('logcosh','cube','exp'):
  for seed in range(8): s,b,mean,iters = fastica(z_all, fun=fun, seed=seed)  # report BEST, an attacker restarts
  check iters vs max_iter (separates 'attack failed' from 'optimiser failed')
feeds: abs-pcorr, pos-pcorr, energy-correlation corr(s_i^2,s_j^2), raw-corr once as the null
add a participation-ratio localisation metric that credits localised-but-not-pixel filters
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Matched energy 0.05-0.25 vs a 0.0123 floor and a 0.25-0.45 ZCA ceiling; edge precision < 0.35; T1 error worse than the honest MLP. A negative result about one contrast, NOT evidence the defence holds.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 5-30 s per unmix on CPU; the QAP dominates -- replace the single 120 s point with a {2,10,30,120} s curve and gate it on a cheap kNN screen. ~90 min for the screened grid.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (as the calibrated baseline the stronger blind attacks are measured against)

ranked_attacks.name: Ambiguity-robust (nuisance-augmented) smuggled CNN -- the multiplier
ranked_attacks.target: n/a -- scoring-side control that re-prices every partial recovery
ranked_attacks.mechanism: The residual ambiguity after any whitened-domain attack is a structured, simulable nuisance: a near-ZCA local mixing, a dihedral, small rotations inside near-degenerate subspaces, swaps among statistically similar pixels. Train the offline CNN on that simulated posterior so it is invariant to exactly what the attack cannot resolve. A CNN is already dihedral-tolerant, so orientation need not be recovered at all.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: offline: xb = (x - mu) @ B.T with B = ZCA_eps @ dihedral @ small_orth_perturb, sampled per batch\nmeasure on the ORACLE ZCA basis: err(clean pixel CNN) vs err(augmented CNN). One number.\nthen re-score every Stage-3/4 attack with the augmented net substituted for the clean one
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Augmented net within 1.0 pp of the clean pixel CNN on the oracle ZCA basis. If confirmed, control_zca_whitening is the attacker's TARGET, not a comforting ceiling, and 'ICA only reached ZCA' stops being a defence.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~30 min offline training; zero extra submission cost.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (it sets the exchange rate between partial basis recovery and end-to-end error)

ranked_attacks.name: Known-marginal / quantile matching on the Stiefel manifold
ranked_attacks.mechanism: After self-whitening only R remains. Match the 81 empirical marginals of Rz against the known whitened-pixel marginals, which are highly individuated at 9x9 (a corner is a near-delta at 0, a centre pixel is broad). Crucially this needs NO independence assumption -- exactly where FastICA is handicapped, since pixels are strongly dependent by construction. Zero-inflation and the [0,1] bound are universal to non-negative image data, so much of it should transfer to a held-out different-source draw.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
H_ref = smuggled 81x32 int8 quantiles; Z = selfwhiten(z_all)
for it in range(2000): Y = Z @ cayley(Q); loss = |sorted_quantiles(Y) - H_ref| ; + lam*relu(-(Y@Winv.T+mu))**2
  re-match coordinates to reference marginals by Hungarian every 25 steps; retract on the Stiefel manifold
seed from the DCT / class-mean / eps-tail estimate rather than random
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Matched energy 0.3-0.6 on a same-source draw, retaining >= 60% of that on a held-out 9x9 source. Should clearly beat FastICA-logcosh head to head; that comparison is what tells you whether the current harness is measuring the strong attack or the weak one.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 1-5 s GPU / ~2 min CPU per cell; 2.6 KB artifact; ~40 min for the headline cells.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (and it is one of the two attacks that informs the hold-out design)

ranked_attacks.name: Blind sparse-precision / DCT lattice-prior basis recovery
ranked_attacks.mechanism: In the pixel basis the precision matrix of 9x9 pixels is nearly lattice-supported (~5 non-zeros per row; topology.py measures edge precision >= 0.99). Under rotation-only the attacker searches R in O(81) making (R Cov(z) R^T)^{-1} sparse, seeded by matching the released eigenvectors to the 2-D DCT basis by eigenvalue rank. After whitening the precision is exactly I for every R, so the objective is identically flat -- the cleanest demonstration of what whitening buys against a blind attacker.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
Th = inv(cov(z) + 1e-4*I)
R0 = V[:, ::-1] @ dct2_basis(9).T  # fit rho of a separable Markov lattice to the eigenvalue profile
for sweep: minimise offdiag-L1(R Th R.T)/||.||_F + nonneg penalty, Givens or Stiefel retraction, 50 restarts
report the achieved objective on rot AND on zca_eps0+rot (must collapse to the flat value)
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Good-to-excellent on rot (the lattice GMRF has a unique very-sparse representation up to signed permutation); exactly chance on any white arm. Establishes that rotation-only is broken even blind, independently of the informed eigen-match.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 1-5 s GPU / ~60 s CPU per cell; zero bytes; ~30 min.

ranked_attacks.name: Class-mean orthogonal Procrustes (810-byte anchor) + provenance test
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Labels give the correspondence for free: R = UV^T from the SVD of sum_c p_c m_c n_c^T. The 10 centred class means span only 9 dimensions, so R is exact there and free on the other 72 -- not a standalone win (that is just LDA), but the correct initialiser that makes the class-covariance and cumulant optimisations near-deterministic. Bonus: the class-mean Gram is an exact rotation invariant, so it both recovers a permuted class labelling and tells the submission whether it is on a public-source draw or the hold-out.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: M = class means of selfwhiten(z_train); N = smuggled 810 B class means (whitened)\nR0 = U @ Vt from svd(M.T @ N)  ; hand R0 to the class-covariance / cumulant attacks\nprovenance: |Gram(M) - Gram(N)| < TOL  ->  switch to the norm-matching attack; else fall back
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: 9 directions at |cos| > 0.99, standalone reconstruction R^2 ~0.2-0.4 and near-failing standalone CNN. Value is the initialiser effect: predicted to raise the class-covariance attack's success rate from < 50% of random restarts to > 90%. Provenance test predicted 10/10 class-permutation recovery and clean separation of source vs hold-out draws.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: < 1 ms; 810 B + 162 B; 10 min including the initialiser ablation.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (measured as an initialiser effect, not as a standalone recovery)

ranked_attacks.name: JADE / third-cumulant Procrustes on the Stiefel manifold (label-free)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Cumulant matrices satisfy Q_z(R M R^T) = R Q_x(M) R^T; matching a family of probes gives ~88k order-3 equations against 3,240 unknowns. Unlike blind ICA this does not require the pixel basis to be the maximally-independent one -- only that the two clouds share a distribution up to R. That is what makes it, rather than sample matching, the attack that could survive a held-out draw from a similar 9x9 source.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
def Qmat(Z,M): w = ((Z@M)*Z).sum(1); return (Z*w[:,None]).T@Z/len(Z) - M - M.T - trace(M)*I
probes = 81 rank-1 + 100 random symmetric; Qz = [Qmat(zw,M)]; minimise sum ||Qz - R Qx R.T||^2 over O(81)
artifact: rank-truncated Qx (top-16 eigenpairs x 24 probes ~ 8 KB) or the public JADE mixing matrix (6.7 KB int8)
sweep N in {5k,10k,20k,40k} to locate the 5d^2 threshold; run on the held-out 9x9 source
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Matched energy 0.3-0.6, comparable to the class-covariance attack rather than better; predicted to retain >= 40% of it on a held-out different-source draw. Full order-4 matching is hopeless at n=20k (1.93M free entries) and should not be attempted.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 10-30 ms GPU / a few minutes CPU per cell; 8 KB artifact; ~40 min.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 3 (specifically whether the planned hold-out draw actually helps)

ranked_attacks.name: Dual-path adaptive submission (escalation ladder + harness audit)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Nothing forces a submission to commit. Run the 810 B class-mean Gram provenance test, then the cheapest applicable recovery, validate on held-out rows of its own labelled split, and fall back to an honest learner if validation is poor. Under an energy-at-fixed-accuracy ranking the optimal play is cheapest-first escalation, so the scheme's security is min over attacks, not the security of the attack the organiser happened to test.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
if provenance_is_public(...): Q = procrustes_from_norm_matching(...)   # ~10 ms
else: Q = eps_tail_anchor(...); Q = atom_facet_refine(..., seed=Q)      # ~1 ms then ~1 s
acc = validate(smuggled_cnn, X_tr[-2000:], y[-2000:]); pred = smuggled_cnn(X_te) if acc>THRESH else honest(...)
AUDIT (not a maths experiment): does the scored container have network access or MNIST on disk? is Q redrawn per scored run? does a dev/practice phase share the final Q? how many adaptive probes does an entrant get?
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Converts every probabilistic attack into a no-downside option at a few hundred joules against a 1200 s budget. The audit questions can invalidate the whole study: with network access or on-disk MNIST the 20 KB cap is decorative.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: Sum of the rungs, ~1-5 s; the audit is free.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 1,2,3 (it determines whether per-attack security numbers compose at all)

ranked_attacks.name: FOBI / kurtosis-matrix eigen-matching, and its bootstrap-covariance-fluctuation twin
ranked_attacks.mechanism: K = E[||z||^2 z z^T] is equivariant (K_z = R K_x R^T) and is NOT killed by whitening, so the same eigen-Procrustes as the rotation-only attack applies with K in place of Sigma. The bootstrap form -- resample rows, take the covariance of the vectorised sample covariances, trace-contract -- carries the same fourth-order information with no cumulant algebra, and is the version a competitor is most likely to actually write. Both make vivid that 'Cov(z)=I exactly' does not mean the second-order statistic is a constant: its SAMPLING DISTRIBUTION still carries the fourth-order channel.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
zw = selfwhiten(z_all); w = (zw**2).sum(1); Kz = (zw*w[:,None]).T @ zw / len(zw)
dz,Vz = eigh(Kz); S = sign(skew(zw@Vz)*smuggled_skew); R = (Vz*S) @ smuggled_Vx.T
bootstrap twin: 500 resampled covariances -> Cov(vec) -> trace-contract -> same eigh (validates the equivalence)
diagnostic that predicts success: relative gaps of the generalised-kurtosis spectrum vs 1/sqrt(N_eff)
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Initialiser-grade: top 10-20 directions at |cos| > 0.9, the rest lost in near-degenerate clusters (whitened MNIST's generalised-kurtosis spectrum is poorly separated, and fourth moments give N_eff ~ 2-5k rather than 20k). Bootstrap version should match the analytic one up to bootstrap noise -- run both only to confirm that equivalence, then keep the analytic one.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~1 ms analytic / ~60 s CPU bootstrap; 1.6-6.7 KB artifact; ~20 min.

ranked_attacks.name: Sliced-Wasserstein / Gromov-Wasserstein distribution alignment
ranked_attacks.mechanism: Both clouds are isotropic after self-whitening and differ by a rotation plus dataset shift, so align them by sliced-W2 over random 1-D projections (differentiable in R) or by entropic GW on intra-cloud distance matrices, which use only Q-invariants and need no anchor. Unlike exact sample matching it degrades gracefully on a different-but-similar source. Defensively notable: because the cost uses only pairwise distances, whitening, eps and truncation change nothing.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch:
U = sample from a smuggled 24-component whitened GMM (~2 KB) or 200 int4 archetypes (16 KB)
for it in range(300): theta = random unit dirs; loss = mean (sort(ZR theta) - sort(U theta))^2 ; Stiefel step
GW variant: T = entropic_gw(pdist(Z_sub), pdist(U_sub)); R = procrustes(Z_sub, T @ U_sub)
run twice: same-source (expect near-exact R, i.e. the known hole recovered as a MAP not just labels) and held-out source
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Near-exact on a same-source draw (subsumes the norm-matching hole); matched energy 0.2-0.5 on a held-out source, enough to seed the marginal-matching pipeline. Failure mode is local minima, so restart count is the ablation axis.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 1-20 s GPU per cell; 2-16 KB artifact (a stored reference cloud blows the cap, so the GMM form is the shippable one); ~30 min.

ranked_attacks.name: Discrete-support / quantisation-lattice screen (and its LLL cousin)
ranked_attacks.target: eps=0 and eps>0 releases; killed by pca-k truncation and by dither
ranked_attacks.mechanism: 9x9 area resizing of uint8 MNIST makes every pixel an integer multiple of 1/7140, so raw x lives on a lattice and coarse-support directions have near-atomic projections. Measured by red team 3: corner pixel 0 takes only NINE distinct values across all 60,000 images, versus 45,021 for interior pixel 40. Exact whitening only rescales the atoms, so a Fourier-magnitude or kNN-entropy screen finds the border axes WITHOUT using second-order statistics -- i.e. it defeats the eps=0 release, which the tail-leak attack cannot. Truncation kills it, because the coarse-support directions are exactly the low-variance ones discarded.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: maximise |mean_i exp(2 pi i f w.z_i)| over unit w and frequency f, 256 batched restarts\nkeep directions with magnitude >> 1/sqrt(n); cluster by |cos|; these are the border-pixel axes\nablations: float32 vs rounded-to-1e-3 release (a possibly free mitigation); pca60; dither
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: ~8-17 border axes recovered blind; interior pixels not (best Fourier magnitude for an interior pixel is ~0.10, 25 sigma above the noise floor but too weak to drive an 81-dim search). Its practical value is that rounding the release to ~1e-3 may kill it at no honest cost -- one cell in the grid buys that answer. The LLL/lattice-reduction version should fail outright at d=81 with a ~1e4 condition number; include only as a cheap negative.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 0.3-1 s GPU / a few minutes CPU; zero bytes; ~20 min.
ranked_attacks.decides_question: 1 (it is a second, independent argument that truncation dominates the eps floor)

ranked_attacks.name: Separate-whitening Wishart/fold-bootstrap anisotropy leak (expected negative, needed as a null)
ranked_attacks.mechanism: The intuitive worry is that two independently fitted whiteners hand over two noisy views of the same map, and that the sampling anisotropy Cov(dC_ij) = (Sigma_ik Sigma_jl + Sigma_il Sigma_jk)/n leaks Sigma in the pixel basis. It should fail: if the release is exactly white, fold covariances are Wishart(I), whose distribution is invariant under conjugation by ANY orthogonal matrix, so it carries zero bits about Q; and with separate fitting the attacker observes exactly one realisation, 3,321 numbers constraining 3,321 unknowns with no averaging.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: folds = split(z_train, 20); D = cov per fold - mean; S = mean(D @ D); vals,vecs = eigh(S)\nmatched energy of vecs vs true pixel axes, compared against a synthetic Wishart(I) null through the IDENTICAL pipeline\nsweep eps in {0,1e-3,1e-2}, k=60, B in {5,20,100}
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: Indistinguishable from the null everywhere except eps>0, where it recovers nothing the one-eigh tail attack did not already get at 1/B the cost. Run it so the write-up can dismiss the leak worry on evidence and rest the case against separate whitening on honest-learner breakage instead.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: ~50 ms per cell; zero bytes; 10 min.

ranked_attacks.name: Adjacency-only recovery feeding a graph/permutation-equivariant learner
ranked_attacks.mechanism: An attacker needs only a neighbourhood graph, not an embedding: a GNN or set-transformer with locality-shaped smuggled weights runs on any adjacency structure. Recovering EDGES is a far lower bar than recovering the layout -- topology.py spends most of its machinery (geodesic MDS, ICP, QAP annealing) turning a good kNN graph into a grid, and the energy-correlation kNN graph survives much more noise than the embedding does. Degrades smoothly: adjacency precision 0.3 still gives real locality.
ranked_attacks.implementation_sketch: S = sources from any basis attack; K = corrcoef((S**2).T); nbr = mutual_knn(K, k=4)   # no embedding step\ntrain a smuggled locality-shaped GNN readout on (S_train, y_train, edges); predict on S_query\ncontrols: random 4-regular graph, ORACLE lattice graph, dense MLP  -- the oracle-vs-MLP gap is the hard ceiling
ranked_attacks.expected_effect: The most robust residual attack under weak basis recovery, but its ceiling is the oracle-lattice-GNN vs dense-MLP gap, which at 9x9 with 10k rows is probably small -- so it may 'succeed' as an attack while being worthless on the leaderboard. Measure the ceiling first; if it is near zero, skip the attack.
ranked_attacks.runtime_cost: 1-5 s per cell; 2-6 KB GNN; ~20 min, and only if the Stage-1 gate shows a meaningful conv-over-dense gap.
